red_team_amendments.question: How often does my own attack change my draft, and which attack lands?
red_team_amendments.note: An attack dimension that has never amended anything is either unnecessary or being performed rather than run, and naming which is part of the report. After run 3 (HUBB): CROWDEDNESS_REALITY landed a second time, arguing 99.03% institutional ownership contradicts an UNDISCOVERED label the draft had reframed as settled rather than contested. PRICED_IN_CHECK and CAPTURE_REALITY landed a third straight time, both finding the same shape of problem: a headline number (a claimed gap, a demand narrative) survives only because a category mismatch or an unquantified attribution was not stress-tested. EVIDENCE_BOUNDARY landed a second time, and not on a data gap this time but on a structural defect: HUBB's independence_test.falsification described the conditions that would CONFIRM the dive, the exact polarity error the repairs log first caught on VRT on 2026-08-29, now caught and fixed a second time on a different file, which argues this specific defect class needs a machine check rather than continued reliance on this attack finding it by hand. PRE_MORTEM stays at 1 of 3 rather than inflated: on HUBB, same as MYRG, the market-would-have-been-right question was answerable (continued margin expansion on Hubbell's own established trend) and the verdict was already at WATCH, the floor that gate imposes, so the pre-mortem informed the file without changing the label. Three of three dives amended is now a pattern worth naming plainly: this red team has never once confirmed a draft unchanged, which either means the draft stage is consistently leaving real gaps for the fresh-context pass to find, or the red team is calibrated to always find something. The failure modes have not repeated across dives (VRT: horizon convention; MYRG: base-year outlier and an invented trigger price; HUBB: category-mismatched gap survival, an unverified AI-attribution, an invented trigger threshold, and a falsifier with inverted polarity), which argues for the former reading, but three data points is not enough to rule out the latter.

implied_growth.question: The market-implied CAGR I recorded at dive time, against what was actually delivered by review_by.
implied_growth.note: This grades the reverse DCF itself. Without it the gap table is a format, not a method. Run 1 found the implied column is one point on a horizon curve. Run 2 found the deeper problem: the column also inherits a BASE, and on MYRG that base is FY2025 free cash flow at 2.90x the trailing four-year average. A horizon sensitivity is published on disk; a base sensitivity is not. When these records resolve, grade the solve against the base as well as the horizon, or this channel will keep grading the less important of the two inputs. Run 4 (ANDR.VI) adds the third distinct defect class in this column: after the horizon (VRT) and the base (MYRG), the DISCOUNT RATE. quality.reverse_dcf assumes 9% for a EUR-denominated net-cash Austrian industrial and publishes no sensitivity to it, and the direction matters: a lower rate lowers the implied CAGR and would widen the dive's gap in its own favour. The dive stated the direction and did not touch the number, because section 7 forbids re-solving in session. When these records resolve, the solve should be graded against its discount rate as well as its base and its horizon, or this channel keeps grading the least consequential of the three inputs.

open_records.my_fcf_cagr_note: Written as a number this time, unlike the MYRG and HUBB records, because this dive actually built one rather than comparing a revenue rate to an FCF rate: revenue 9,815.7 MEUR in 2030 at a comparable EBITA margin held flat at 8.6% gives EBITA of 844.2 MEUR against 646.4 MEUR in 2025, a 5.49% CAGR, at unchanged cash conversion. Against the filed 5-year implied 5.3% that is a gap of +0.19pp, inside the file's own 1.21pp horizon_spread, which is why the dive claims NO measurable gap. At the 10-year convention (4.09% implied) the same expectation is +1.40pp ahead, wider than the spread, so the SIGN of the finding depends on the convention; the dive claims the filed 5-year default and says so.
open_records.base_fcf_caveat: 454.6M EUR is FY2025 free cash flow (OCF 652.7M less capex 198.1M) and 1.088x the FY2022-2025 average of 417.9M, so unlike MYRG's 2.90x this base is NOT an outlier year and the check that caught MYRG passes here. The opposite caveat applies instead: group FCF has compounded at -6.48% a year over three years (555.8M in 2022 to 454.6M in 2025), so the 5.3% implied ask is a reversal of the recent trend rather than an extrapolation of it. EV/base FCF is 17.78x; EV over the four-year average is 19.34x, a much smaller spread than MYRG's 19.11x against 55.45x.
